title: Ivo and the Ghost
premise: Vesper Dunmore, a crash investigator haunted by the unexplained death of his family in row twelve of Flight 4471, has spent five years buried in bureaucratic routine. When a stranger named Ivo repays a favor Vesper never performed—delivering a ledger proving row twelve was no accident—he pulls Vesper into a conspiracy spanning three governments and a financial scheme set to detonate when Frankfurt's markets open. Hunted by an assassin who erases witnesses to the crash, Vesper must choose between the safety of invisibility and exposing the truth. In the end, Vesper gets the ledger out with Ivo's sacrifice, the markets open on scandal instead of profit, and he finally grieves his family as a man who knows why they died.
about_author: Hazel Lockridge is a former aviation insurance analyst who left the industry after a decade of reading crash reports no one wanted questioned. She writes thrillers about ordinary people trapped inside systems designed to forget them.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Five years after losing his family in row twelve, Vesper files routine reports and keeps his head down at the Transportation Safety Bureau. Then Ivo appears at his door claiming Vester once saved his life—a debt Vesper has no memory of—and leaves behind a ledger implicating the airline's parent fund in the crash. The beat: dread cracking open a carefully sealed life.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Alternating Vesper and Ivo POVs. As Vesper verifies the ledger's flight data, an assassin begins eliminating former bureau colleagues, and Ivo reveals he was the crash's hired fixer before his conscience turned. They form an uneasy alliance built on guilt and mutual usefulness. The beat: two liars learning to trust, while realizing the assassin is closing in faster than expected.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Bullet
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, shifting to Vesper for the climax. Smuggling the ledger through Vienna toward a regulator who can act before Frankfurt opens, they're betrayed by their contact and ambushed; Ivo takes a bullet buying Vesper the escape window. Cornered in a data center, Vesper broadcasts the ledger publicly rather than trusting any government. The beat: love against duty—Ivo's sacrifice forcing Vesper to stop hiding.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The markets open on collapse as regulators freeze the fund; the assassin is arrested, but Ivo dies before dawn. At the memorial Vesper finally speaks his family's names aloud, no longer invisible, carrying both grief and Ivo's memory forward. The beat: belonging found not in safety, but in truth finally told.
